content:
Assume \(P_0\) is a knight. Then \(P_1,\dots,P_{10}\) are all liars.

For \(P_{11}\), the next 10 clockwise people are exactly \(P_{12},\dots,P_{21}\).

If \(P_{11}\) were a liar, then at least one of \(P_{12},\dots,P_{21}\) would be a knight. But any such knight would have \(P_0\) among its next 10 clockwise people, contradicting that \(P_0\) is a knight. Therefore none of \(P_{12},\dots,P_{21}\) is a knight.

So \(P_{12},\dots,P_{21}\) are all liars, making \(P_{11}\)'s statement true. Hence \(P_{11}\) is a knight.

Thus the only knights are \(P_0\) and \(P_{11}\), so there are \(22-2=20\) liars.

\[
\boxed{20}
\]
